tagline: Strategic investment holding company managing diversified portfolio including core stakes in Volkswagen and Porsche AG, with expanding technology and defense investments
hero_kpi_rationale: Porsche SE manages two key performance indicators: adjusted Group result after tax and consolidated net debt, which directly reflect its strategy of sustainable value creation for shareholders.

kpis.explanation: Core earnings metric reflecting profitability of the Porsche SE Group, adjusted for special factors. Key management KPI as stated in the 2025 annual report.
kpis.description: Porsche SE Group's adjusted net result for fiscal year 2025 amounted to EUR 2.894 billion, down 8.2% compared to the prior year (2024: EUR 3.151 billion). This decrease reflects macroeconomic challenges, protectionist measures (notably US tariffs) and intensified competition affecting core holdings. The result remains a key management indicator for the diversified investment platform.
kpis.signal: Solid core profitability despite challenging macroeconomic environment and geopolitical headwinds

kpis.explanation: Consolidated net debt position of the Porsche SE Group as of December 31, including financial liabilities net of cash and cash equivalents. Key balance sheet metric.
kpis.description: Porsche SE Group's consolidated net debt amounted to EUR 5.099 billion as of December 31, 2025, down slightly by 1.2% compared to December 31, 2024 (EUR 5.160 billion). This improvement reflects successful refinancing measures from the prior year and demonstrates the solidity of the investment platform's financing. Management expects net debt between EUR 4.7 and 5.2 billion as of December 31, 2026.
kpis.signal: Strong financial foundation with stable net debt position and successful refinancing measures

kpis.explanation: NAV represents the aggregate value of Porsche SE's portfolio holdings and other assets less liabilities, reflecting the underlying value of the investment platform.
kpis.description: Porsche SE's Net Asset Value amounted to EUR 17.846 billion as of December 31, 2025, up 4.9% compared to 2024 (EUR 17.019 billion). This increase notably reflects the growing valuation of portfolio holdings, whose book value nearly doubled to approximately EUR 535 million since year-end 2024. Strategic expansion into defense and technology sectors contributes to strengthening long-term value creation potential.
kpis.signal: Growing underlying value of diversified investment portfolio with portfolio holdings book value nearly doubled

kpis.explanation: The holding discount represents the difference between NAV and market capitalization as a percentage of NAV, indicating the market's valuation of the holding company structure.
kpis.description: The holding discount stood at 31% as of December 31, 2025, a significant improvement of 11.4 percentage points compared to 2024 (35%). This discount reduction reflects improved market perception of the holding structure and value creation potential of Porsche SE's diversified investment platform, notably through the success of portfolio holdings achieving unicorn status (valuation of at least EUR 1 billion).
kpis.signal: Narrowing discount reflects improving investor perception of holding company structure and portfolio value creation

kpis.explanation: LTV ratio measures net debt as a percentage of NAV, reflecting the financial leverage of the investment platform and debt capacity.
kpis.description: The LTV ratio (net debt to net asset value) stood at 22.2% as of December 31, 2025, an improvement of 4.7 percentage points compared to 2024 (23.3%). This ratio reflects a comfortable leverage position and demonstrates Porsche SE's financial flexibility to pursue its diversified investment strategy, notably in strategic sectors such as European defense and advanced technologies.
kpis.signal: Comfortable leverage position with improving debt-to-asset ratio, supporting financial flexibility for strategic investments

kpis.explanation: Dividend income received from portfolio investments, primarily from core stakes in Volkswagen AG and Porsche AG, reflecting cash returns on strategic holdings.
kpis.description: Dividends received by Porsche SE during fiscal year 2025 amounted to EUR 1.006 billion, down 40.9% compared to 2024 (EUR 1.703 billion). This decrease reflects reduced distributions from core holdings, notably Volkswagen AG and Porsche AG, due to operational challenges and a difficult macroeconomic environment characterized by geopolitical uncertainties and protectionist measures.
kpis.signal: Dividend income decline reflects reduced distributions from core holdings amid challenging operating environment

kpis.explanation: Total dividend distributions paid to shareholders during the fiscal year, reflecting shareholder remuneration policy.
kpis.description: Dividends paid to Porsche SE shareholders during fiscal year 2025 amounted to EUR 584 million, down 25.4% compared to 2024 (EUR 783 million). Despite a challenging operating environment, management maintains its commitment to shareholders by proposing a distribution for fiscal year 2025 of EUR 1.510 per preference share and EUR 1.504 per ordinary share.
kpis.signal: Dividend payout maintained despite earnings pressures, demonstrating commitment to shareholder returns

kpis.explanation: Annual dividend distribution per preference share for fiscal year 2025, proposed to shareholders for approval at Annual General Meeting.
kpis.description: The proposed dividend per preference share for fiscal year 2025 amounts to EUR 1.510, down 20.9% compared to 2024 (EUR 1.910). This reduction reflects management's cautious approach amid macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties, while maintaining attractive shareholder remuneration. For fiscal year 2026, management expects adjusted result between EUR 1.5 and 3.5 billion.
kpis.signal: Dividend reduction reflects cautious capital allocation amid uncertain macroeconomic outlook for 2026

kpis.explanation: IFRS consolidated net profit of Porsche SE Group including special items and one-time effects from portfolio revaluations.
kpis.description: Porsche SE Group's net result after tax amounted to EUR 2.651 billion for fiscal year 2025, representing an exceptional improvement compared to fiscal year 2024, which recorded a loss of EUR 20.017 billion. This substantial improvement notably reflects the positive revaluation of portfolio holdings, with book value nearly doubled, as well as the absence of impairment charges that had impacted the prior year. The IFRS result includes special items and one-time effects related to portfolio revaluations.
kpis.signal: Significant recovery from prior year loss, reflecting improved valuation of portfolio holdings

kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of EUR 1.91 last year.

kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of EUR 0.584 billion last year.

kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 3 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 22.0% last year.

kpis.explanation: Net income divided by average diluted shares outstanding for the fiscal year. Allows visualization of the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for calculating the Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Conflicts of interest within the supervisory board
risks.summary: Certain members of Porsche SE's supervisory board also serve on the boards of Volkswagen AG and Porsche AG, which can create situations where their personal interests conflict with those of Porsche SE.
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly mentioned mid-report with direct language ('können Interessenkonflikte entstehen'); stable trend, this type of conflict related to dual mandates is structural; governance/key person category has moderate weight but the risk is concrete and documented by a real case in 2025.

risks.title: Impairment of VW and Porsche AG holdings
risks.summary: Porsche SE had to reduce the book value of its holdings in Volkswagen and Porsche AG in 2025, which directly weighs on its accounts and shareholder value.
risks.score_rationale: Risk placed at end of report but highlighted as major discussion topic during audit ('Wesentlicher Diskussionsgegenstand') with strong language; increased trend as non-cash impairments were actually recorded in 2025; capital/valuation category has high weight for a pure holding company.

risks.title: Risk of non-detection of existential threats
risks.summary: The early risk detection system must enable timely identification of any threat that could endanger Porsche SE's survival; its proper functioning is verified annually by auditors.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned mid-report within the audit committee framework with vigilance language ('bestandsgefährdende Risiken frühzeitig zu erkennen'); stable trend, recurring control; operational/industrial risk category has moderate weight but the company survival issue is explicitly mentioned.

risks.title: Tax risk related to tax rate changes
risks.summary: A change in corporate tax rate in Germany requires Porsche SE to recalculate its deferred taxes, which can significantly modify the reported accounting result.
risks.score_rationale: Identified as priority audit item mid-report with precise language ('Bewertung latenter Steuern unter Berücksichtigung der Änderung des Körperschaftsteuersatzes'); new trend as linked to rate change; regulatory/tax category has high weight.

risks.title: Portfolio concentration on two holdings
risks.summary: Porsche SE is a holding company whose nearly entire value rests on two holdings (Volkswagen and Porsche AG); any decline in value of these two assets directly and massively impacts the company's financial position.
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk present throughout the report, with factual but revealing language ('Werthaltigkeitstests der Beteiligungen an der Volkswagen AG sowie der Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG'); stable trend but aggravated by 2025 impairments; capital category has high weight for a holding whose value depends almost exclusively on two assets.

ai_positioning.summary: Porsche SE supports the strategic integration of AI and defense technologies through its holdings in Volkswagen and Porsche AG, as well as through its expansion into European technology startup financing. The emphasis is on incremental innovation and strategic diversification rather than direct disruption.
evidence: Growing investments in European technology startups through DTCP's Defense Fund (EUR 100 million in 2026)
Focus on software solutions, cybersecurity and autonomous systems in the defense sector
Indirect AI support through autonomous vehicles and digital services at Porsche AG and Volkswagen
Six portfolio holdings having achieved unicorn status (valuation exceeding EUR 1 billion)

events.title: Waabi raises up to $1 billion and partners with Uber to deploy 25,000 robotaxis as the race to dominate self-driving hea
events.body: The AI company, which had been focused on software to enable autonomous trucking, has now expanded into robotaxis.
